reason: Owns the shared built-in argument parser: next/remaining, typed value decoding, unknown-argument collection, one refusal message shape. Every built-in request parser uses it, so flag semantics cannot drift per command.
One generic seam for help-then-parse-then-execute, plus the passthrough variant that refuses verbose-root/env-schema for built-ins. Removes the repeated three-step shape from every arm.
Owns the completion command entry: help vs export vs install, shell/action resolution and prompt policy. Delegates each mechanism to a named submodule.
Owns selector candidate generation and the manifest cache (TTL policy, per-manifest parse). Proof is thin: 2 local tests, mean 6.5, one at 6.
Small help text owner for completion; static content, no branching.

Owns completion install: managed block markers, startup file edit, install plan/result types. Proof is thin (3 tests, mean 7, one at 6) for a mechanism that edits a user's shell startup file, so a failed-edit control is worth adding.
Owns completion export/install response rendering; one text path and one schema payload per action.
Owns interactive shell/action prompting through the shared PromptPolicy. Proof is thin (3 tests, mean 7.33, one at 6).
Owns completion argument decoding (action flags, shell, candidates prefix) into typed requests.

Owns the generated bash/zsh/fish scripts and their command index. Ownership deduction: crates/effigy-builtin/src/completion/scripts/command_index.rs builds a third command-name inventory (BUILTIN_TASKS plus EXTRA_DIRECT_COMMANDS plus surface option constants) beside effigy_cli::command_surface and builtin_names.
Owns the `config` command entry and the nested `config completion` route; delegates rendering and parsing.

Owns the config documentation corpus (reference and schema profiles). Typed-fact deduction: the text restates the manifest schema by hand instead of deriving from the types, so it can drift. Only the tasks section and the secrets example are loaded back through the loader; the assembled template is only string-matched.

Owns config command rendering: inspect payloads with composition edges/overrides, user-config text/TOML/JSON, schema and reference payloads. Large but single-purpose; 9 integration tests cover schema/inspect output.
Owns the human reference rendering, section by section; presentation only.
Owns config request decoding into a typed ConfigRequest plus the user-key enum; single grammar for inspect/schema/path/get/set/unset.

Owns the canonical/minimal schema template. Typed-fact deduction: the "strict-valid" template is assembled by hand from section text, and no test loads the assembled whole through the manifest loader. Proportion: 272 lines of concatenation plus per-target switch arms.
Small doc-rendering helpers. Ownership deduction: hash-comment muting exists twice, once as a whole-string transform and once as a per-line emit, so a change to the muting rule must be made in both.
Owns the doctor request grammar and delegates the report to the runtime port; typed request, ports boundary unchanged.
Typed built-in error boundary mirroring runner variants one-for-one, with a documented lift at the edge; failures keep their class instead of becoming strings.
Owns `effigy help` argument decoding and delegates rendering to the CLI help owner, so help facts have one source.
Tiny section renderer shared by built-in help panels.
Owns the init entry: mode selection, starter emission, dry-run/overwrite record. Delegates wizard, inventory and output.

Owns agent-contract emission: managed block markers, embedded contract text, idempotent insert/replace. Deductions: the contract text is an embedded copy that only text assertions guard, and 1041 lines mix block editing with job execution.
Owns setup inventory: detection context, job catalogue with categories/safety classes, and execution of selected actions; typed job model.
Owns init result rendering (per-file emission, JSON schema payload).
Owns init argument decoding into typed InitMode/AgentInitMode, keeping retired spellings refused.
Owns the interactive init wizard phases over the same job inventory; prompt decisions come from PromptPolicy. Proof is thin (2 tests, mean 7.5) and the interactive path is hard to exercise.
Owns the built-in dispatch entry and the "which built-in would run" predicate; thin root over the registry with no hidden logic.

Owns the runtime port trait: lock scopes, suite custody, child evidence. Ownership/typed-fact deduction: the lock guard is deliberately type-erased (`Box<dyn Any + Send>`), so the type system cannot say what the built-in holds.
One typed prompt policy with an explicit suppression reason for every mode; no ad-hoc tty checks elsewhere.
Owns the built-in registry table and dispatch; a drift test keeps the table aligned with the built-in task list.
Owns built-in response shaping: text-or-JSON choice, schema envelope with version, lazy fields. Single owner of the payload envelope.
Owns the `scan` entry: help on empty args, candidate mode, delegation to the request/execution split.
Owns scan execution: typed mode config, threshold overrides, payload/response building and fail-on-findings mapping. Splits api/overrides/payloads/response cleanly.
Owns scan help panels through the shared help_text renderer; static content.
Owns scan argument parsing into typed ScanRequest/ScanCommand, including retired subcommand refusal and positive-integer thresholds.
Owns shared built-in runtime-arg refusals, unknown-argument messages and help-flag detection; no duplicated flag scanning.
Owns the `tasks` built-in entry and request decoding; listing rendering lives in effigy-tasks.
Owns the built-in test entry: flag extraction, plan mode, target/suite routing and child evidence. Delegates execution to one of two runners.

Owns test suite execution: TUI session and parallel runner, sweep custody, per-suite command rendering and child evidence. Proportion deduction: two full execution paths (TUI and parallel) each build specs, run and collect results, and shell blocks are assembled by string concatenation.

Owns built-in test flag extraction, target/runnable models, config and scope composition (auto `--workspace` yields to explicit selection). Typed decisions throughout; crates/effigy-builtin/src/test/planning/scope.rs documents the exact refusal.
Owns target resolution: workspace/catalog targets, cargo env matching, per-target plan resolution. Single resolver used by both plan and execution.
Owns test plan rendering (text, payload, projection). One projection feeds both renderings.

Owns suite result rendering and hints. Proportion: crates/effigy-builtin/src/test/render/results.rs carries render paths, env-file sections and hint logic in 266 lines; consolidated with payload/hint it is near 480 lines for one rendering surface.
Owns the pure storage requirement derived from the same suite resolver used by execution, so plan and run cannot disagree.
Owns suite selection with a typed error carrying available runners; one refusal path.
Owns the suite sweep: one token, read kernel state once after the last suite, TERM then KILL, fail naming the token. Custody behaviour is explicit and bounded.
Trivial line-builder used by doc rendering; single owner, tested.
Single typed table for which authority owns a built-in word; shadowing, parse deferral and escape spellings all derive from it and a drift test guards the route list. Small, focused, no duplication.

Owns the top-level grammar and decodes it into Command. Deduction: parse_tasks maintains a second flag table and re-serialises raw argv for the built-in tasks, and the per-command loops repeat the same repo/json/help shape across 12 files.
One grammar for bootstrap, with retired spellings refused by name and a typed shape guess kept explicit. Clear failure messages; covered by local and integration parse tests.
Four small subcommand parsers into typed ChangelogSubcommand; uniform, no special cases beyond per-verb flags.

Owns the largest command family: about 30 container subcommands with bounded u64 parsing and typed profile/cache/volume enums. Deduction: the bare-target predicates are duplicated with slightly different rules, and 1.5k lines of hand-written loops carry the surface.
One grammar per deploy verb into typed args; env-read sharing is factored through parse_env_read_command.
Typed DocsCheckKind decoding with a single named invalid-kind message and per-check requirements kept as typed lists.
Small, explicit file-set parser for the fmt escape route; single owner, no branching beyond flag recognition.
One parser per release verb; stages, decisions and receipts stay typed rather than string-matched downstream.
Owns gateway/system/workspace/exec/service grammars, including address parsing and the retired gateway verbs' refusal text.
Small typed secrets grammar; the import/export/read helpers keep key parsing in one place.

Owns state/history/plan/apply/capture/artifact grammar into typed variants. Typed-fact deduction: looks_like_manifest_path guesses whether a positional is a manifest path from separators and a .toml suffix, and the caller then branches on that guess.

Owns the help inventory and the named-skill selector refusal. Ownership deduction: four parallel tables describe the same command surface (COMMAND_DESCRIPTORS, HELP_COMMAND_TOPICS, GENERAL_HELP_ENTRIES, HELP_COMMAND_BUILTIN_ROUTES), each carrying names and topics by hand; parity tests defend pairs but a new command still needs several edits.

Owns global flag stripping and propagation. Typed-fact deduction: whether a task already carries a flag is re-derived by scanning raw argv strings, and three open matches over Command repeat per-variant propagation. Two strippers exist (strip_global_cli_flags and the json-only strip_global_json_flags).

Owns the CLI banner. Reads NO_COLOR/EFFIGY_COLOR/EFFIGY_BROWSER_TERMINAL_COLS and falls back to crossterm sizing; local tests cover truncation and width growth, but colour rendering is only checked indirectly from CLI tests.
Owns topic rendering through a narrow HelpRenderer trait and the topic registry; keeps the CLI free of the heavy UI surface. No duplication found beyond the surface tables noted in command_surface.
One module group holding the typed help panels; each panel is static presentation data with a single owner. High churn (102 commits in 90 days) is documentation text, not mechanism growth.

Owns the typed CLI command tree and the parse entrypoint; every command is a typed variant so callers never re-read argv. Proportion deduction: five doc-hidden internal IPC verbs live inside the operator grammar, so internal plumbing and the public surface share one enum.

Owns targeted usage for argument errors. Typed-fact deduction: it re-derives each command's grammar by parsing rendered help text into tokens, so the hint silently follows panel wording and flag spellings.
Tiny shared value decoders used by every parser; single owner of required-value and bool-literal refusal.
Owns the typed task-execution request/plan: route resolution, preflight/discovery/selection/binding plans and diagnostics. One request type, exhaustive route enum, errors carry the offending field.
Owns the bounded QA-group run record: versioned schemas, explicit Unknown outcome never reported as a pass, separate group identity.
Owns bundle spec/input resolution and the source-root/relocation facts; typed BundleInputSpec rather than string paths. Integration tests cover bundle config and local bundles.
Local-only source resolution and progress reporting; refuses to touch a checkout it does not own.
The single source updater: one Prepare owner, one lock, staging directory plus one rename so a shared path is never read half-written. Complex, but the complexity is the contract.
Owns include/extend/overlay composition with provenance maps, evaluation order, override records and cycle detection. Deep but proportionate to composition semantics; 32 local tests.
Facade that names the config-section surface and hosts cross-section tests; no mechanism of its own.
Owns the [bootstrap] config shape and pinned-source declaration. Duplicate validation with crates/effigy-manifest/src/sources.rs is recorded there; this side is the deserialize shape.
Owns [bundle]/catalog-source config shape with typed enums; no failure path beyond serde.

Owns the largest config section (containers, systems, workspace, data targets). Proportion: 751 lines of structs/enums with cross-field validation split into crates/effigy-manifest/src/lib.rs; the surface is genuinely large, but kebab aliases and inline-vs-named variants keep accruing.
Tiny typed [contracts] section; no branching.
Owns docs-policy config including the graph kinds/currentness model and committed-source loading; validates with named failures.
Typed release targets/gates/identity; keeps release config facts as enums rather than strings.
Typed secrets backend/vault/external config plus retired vault-key refusal with the replacement message.
Resolves a task's host/workspace/container binding once into typed ResolvedTaskExecutionBinding, with one error type naming the conflicting declaration. Single owner of binding resolution.
Owns manifest ingress: provenance map, retired-config scan, normalise, deserialize-then-validate. Small and singular.
Owns the v0.15 kebab-case alias window and records one notice per form; bounded by design and time-limited.

Owns the manifest shape, top-level key inventory and load-time validation with action-oriented messages. Typed-fact deduction: [deploy] and [state] stay raw toml Value by intent, so their facts are re-decoded by the runner rather than owned here.
One strict date type: shape check, real-calendar refusal, canonical rendering. Single owner, tested behaviours.
Owns the loaded-catalog/task-selection shapes moved out of the runner so managed can depend on them; data plus small constructors.
Owns [manifest] include/extend/minimum-version config and the version gate; the +local bypass is explicit and documented.
Owns the deliberately tiny portfolio grammar with unknown-key refusal; no crawler behaviour.
Owns the bounded QA-group grammar: typed lifecycle/scope/member kinds, scope-token matching, one refusal per invalid form.

Translates retired [bootstrap] spellings into the current setup/start shape and records notices; time-limited compat. Proportion: a 507-line value-rewriting pass that will be deleted in v0.16, so its size is bounded by the deadline.
Owns the one per-manifest retirement declaration and its notice/refusal text; single collection point.
Owns the manifest Deserialize bridge that applies retirement passes and refuses [drafts]/draft with replacements. Refusal-not-ignore for task-defining keys is the right failure direction.
Owns retirement-notice delivery: per-invocation channel, per-checkout digest marker, nested suppression. Write failure keeps the notice rather than losing it.
Owns dropping removed sections whose loss changes nothing else, recording each in the declaration; [drafts] stays refused in retired_keys.

Owns pinned-source inspection and acquisition: pin resolution, drift states, staging clone plus one rename, no reset/fetch/clean. Deduction: rev/rev_file exclusivity and plain-handle validation are implemented twice, here and in crates/effigy-manifest/src/lib.rs, with different code paths.
Owns task-definition deserialization (shorthand vs table, sequences, visibility); one deserializer, typed results.

Owns task runtime shapes (managed runs, env, profiles, visibility). Deductions: `mode` is a free string re-compared in nine places across runner and builtin code, and retired start_after_ms is accepted but ignored for ordering while its delay still applies, so one field means two things in the v0.15 window.
Owns [test] suites and teardown policy types, with the removed tasks.test story handled in lib validation.
Owns ~/.effigy/config.toml load/save and the test-home override. Proof is thin: 12 local tests, 8 at score 6 or below, and no integration test drives save/load through a real binary.
Owns host API registration order and the shared Rhai<->Rust conversion helpers (`rhai_runtime_error`, `resolve_runtime_path`, temp dirs). One seam, all module builders called from here.

Owns the `container::` module surface. Typed-fact deduction: results are re-encoded into Rhai string maps (`serde_json::json!` plus Map), so failure and data shape are conveyed as dynamic values, though the callbacks themselves are typed.
Thin `exec::` surface over the typed execution crate with a cwd mapper and path refusal helpers; no duplicated execution logic.
Owns the `effigy::` core feature surface (task/state/scanner entrypoints) and delegates to the registered feature runners.
Owns the remaining `effigy::` feature modules, including the secrets module built with its policy context.
Owns the `forge::` surface over a forge CLI. Typed-fact deduction: the forge result is parsed from JSON into dynamic maps and status is re-derived from text fields.
Owns the `fs::` surface including staged no-clobber publishing, SHA-256 and dotenv entry edits; custody helpers are explicit and refuse on failure.
Owns the `git::` surface; each call runs one git command and returns a typed map via the shared process map helper.
Owns the `http::` surface with bounded timeout and a write-failure helper; network work delegated to network_support.
Owns the `process::` surface, delegating spawn options and recursive-Effigy refusal to process_support.
Owns the `prompt::` surface, refusing when not a terminal instead of hanging.
Owns the `search::` surface; one native fn over the bounded search helper.
Owns the `semver::` surface over typed `semver::Version`/`VersionReq`, returning typed booleans/maps.
Owns the `state::` surface over state JSON payloads; typed at the callback boundary.
Owns the pure utility modules (time/path/url/json/toml/yaml/str/random/regex). Each builder is small and returns typed values; no duplication with the CLI.

Owns the Rhai engine seam: parser limits, script context, secret policy, host registration, redaction and the complexity hint. Deductions: four stacked `execute_rhai_script_*` wrappers each forward to the next, and error classification is done by matching Rhai's message text.
Owns bounded file search and HTTP request execution with typed option structs; single implementation behind two surfaces.
Owns process spawn mapping, the recursive-Effigy refusal and PTY handling shared by `process::` and `effigy::`; one owner for spawn policy.

Owns Rhai secret access policy (targets/refuse, local-dev vs vault, session provider) and also a hand-written Rhai source scanner used only to decide whether a vault is opened. Deductions: three mechanisms in one file, and the scanner re-implements Rhai lexing (comments, strings, interpolation) whose drift would silently change secret exposure.
Owns the published host surface: module names, feature descriptors and rendered signatures that `rhai surface` prints; single typed inventory.

Crate-boundary error type. Deductions: it has one Message(String) variant, so every caller loses the failure class, and From<UiError> stringifies a typed UI error at the boundary. The message text is still actionable, but nothing can branch on the kind.
Owns the task-domain trait, context and runtime-arg value type, and re-exports the task surfaces; a value-type root with no hidden logic.

Owns task inventory projection and both renderings from one typed result (`ListTasksResult`), so text and JSON cannot drift. 903 lines are projection plus stable payload shaping, with integration tests for listings and JSON.
Owns selector parsing/rendering glue and task runtime-arg parsing, including the task-args boundary rule. Typed args out, no re-scan by callers.
Small, single-purpose: managed-profile facts for `tasks --resolve`. Explicitly notes selector resolution has one owner in the runner, so it does not duplicate resolution.
Owns the `tasks qa-groups list` projection with one versioned payload and no implicit discovery.
Owns the pure QA-group surface: selection restricted to the group surface, member resolution, typed scope comparison, definition digests. Execution is left to the runner.
Owns non-executing plan resolution and admission shape: typed scope match, exact planner reasons, no run ID on needs_planner.
Owns QA-group text/JSON rendering from the typed plan. Proof is thin: 3 local tests (mean 6.67, one at 6) and the payload shape is asserted mainly through CLI integration tests.

Owns task-reference word splitting and selectors. Typed-fact deduction: it hand-writes a shell-like tokenizer (quotes, escapes) whose result is then re-split by rules the shell already owns, and its error channel is String.
Owns test-runner detection value types and the public route entrypoint; the runners are split by language.
Owns the Oxide route: pool-describe proof, no silent fallback, refusal names the plain-Cargo escape. Process-wide route cache is explicit.
Owns Rust runner detection (nextest vs cargo test, workspace probe) with evidence strings per candidate. Clear ownership, no duplicated routing.

Owns Vitest detection. Deductions: it hand-rolls a JS lexer (comments, strings, regex literals, balanced objects) to read `test.dir` out of a config, and a config that is present but unparsable silently yields no `--dir` and no evidence note, so the run silently widens to the repo root.

Owns task display rows and previews shared by listing and help. Typed-fact deduction: `task_run_preview` and profile eligibility re-read `mode`/`profile` string fields on the manifest task instead of a resolved binding.
Owns one visibility policy across inventory, help and completion; resolves references through the routing owner and hides nothing on a miss.

Shared TUI value types (log entries, exit state, input mode, index helpers). Ownership deduction: it re-declares the Effigy palette as its own ANSI-256 constants instead of using effigy_ui::theme, so two palettes drift independently.
Owns optional runtime diagnostics (env-gated counters and a bounded trace ring). Pure instrumentation with no product decision; no local test asserts its counters.
Owns input dispatch and process-event handling (stdout/stderr/chunk/exit), split into one handler per event kind. Event handling appends to the session's own logs rather than re-deriving state.
Owns command-mode key dispatch and shell shortcuts; one handler per key class, with pre-dispatch decisions named separately.
Owns terminal init/restore, shutdown progress and the final session summary; the session's recorded entry state is the outcome authority.
Owns the multi-process TUI entry, options, session outcome types and control callback. Delegates events/render/state; single public seam.

Owns frame layout, tabs, footer and overlays. Proof is thin at this level: crates/effigy-tui/src/multiprocess/render.rs itself has no local test module (the panes submodule carries the tests), so layout composition is only exercised through rendering snapshots.
Owns output/input/shell-cursor pane rendering with a tested frame snapshot. Dead-code note: `active_vt` is kept only to avoid touching call sites.
Owns the event loop tick: control poll, event drain, view-model build, render. Single loop with one test; the loop's timing behaviour is hard to assert in-process.
Owns session preparation: terminal init, PTY sizing env, process spec decoration before the loop.
Owns session state: per-process logs, scroll/follow, startup state, VT parsers, options actions. Single state container with accessors and tests.
Owns transcript rendering and export into `.effigy/exports`; bounded to the active process and ensures the export dir is ignored.
Owns the render view model: plain vs VT scroll view, scrollbar totals, shell cursor, snapshot of active state. Keeps render code free of state mutation.
Owns terminal-text plumbing: config limits, elapsed formatting, sanitation, payload ingest and bounded log buffers. One ingest path feeds both TUI and transcript.
Owns ANSI payload normalization: escape-sequence parse, cursor-up handling, styled spans. Isolated parser with its own tests.
Owns log payload ingestion into bounded buffers and generation boundaries; one normalise-then-sanitise path.
Owns the live VT terminal buffer with a UTF-8 carry across chunks; single parser owner for live rendering.
Owns VT scrollback-to-LogEntry projection and clamped offsets; follow/clamp decisions are explicit.
Owns the one human error renderer: failure, bounded and redacted evidence, next action, rendered as text and as the same facts in JSON. Single owner with explicit bounds; 14 behaviour tests.
Crate root plus the published style helper. Ownership deduction: `style_text` exists four times - here, in plain_renderer, in effigy-tasks/src/view.rs and inline in effigy-cli/src/header.rs.

Owns renderer constructors, JSON encoding, UTF-8 conversion and the JSON-aware colour policy. Ownership deduction: its `resolve_text_color_enabled` repeats theme::resolve_color_enabled under another name; the canonical policy should be theme's.
Owns the plain Renderer implementation: sections, notices, message blocks, lists, tables, step lines. Single implementation behind the trait.
Owns the Renderer trait and `UiError`; widget types stay in effigy-core, so the trait is the single contract every renderer implements.

Owns step progress: one process-wide sink, spinner and plain modes, capture, streaming and terminal suspension. Proportion deduction: five mechanisms share one 1450-line file, and the sink is process-global mutable state with env-detected modes.
Owns table rendering with fixed padding; one byte-exact test pins the v0.13 shape.

Owns the palette and OutputMode from EFFIGY_COLOR. Ownership deduction: the colour-enable decision is duplicated in crates/effigy-ui/src/output.rs, and effigy-cli/header.rs re-reads EFFIGY_COLOR/NO_COLOR itself instead of going through OutputMode.

Owns execution-request assembly from a selection/preflight: effective runtime inputs, environment plan, request builder. Proportion deduction: 765 lines of builder glue plus re-export indirection for the binding types.

Resolves a task's container/workspace binding into a runner-owned enum with policy loading and exec cwd. Ownership deduction: it defines `ExecutionBindingKind` with exactly the variants effigy_execution already owns, and wraps that shared kind in a second `ExecutionBindingResolution`, so the same fact has two types.
Owns the per-task execution context (resolved target, selector, selection, repo root, command) derived once from preflight; no re-derivation by callers.
Owns the manifest-task request entry: run-key stripping, preflight build, plan refusal and local-dev secret activation before routing.

Owns scoped backing-service alias resolution for host runs, refusing when this checkout has no published service rather than silently reaching another scope's database. Proportion: 519 lines combine alias resolution, env precedence and the gateway route read.
Owns the task run/plan JSON payloads and the planned runtime target, explicitly sharing the execution target so `--plan` cannot disagree with execution.
Owns execution pipeline dispatch between command, standard and managed paths. Typed-fact deduction: every branch keys off the manifest task's `mode` string.

Owns managed-run execution: environment plan, tabs, gateway startup, exec markers, secret access and inline-environment release. Deductions: the highest-churn module in the domain (109 commits/90d, 8 fixes) and 2230 lines of special cases keyed off `mode` strings; several helpers exist only for one branch (`should_open_workspace_shell_for_non_managed_task`, `managed_setup_steps_can_run_locally`).

Owns standard (host/container) task execution: routing wrapper, secret resolution by scanning run shell, workspace shell and teardown. Deductions: it detects required secret env names by lexing raw shell text, and re-implements vault-path/passphrase reading beside the secrets crate helpers.
Owns the execution preflight value (invocation as typed, resolved target, discovery plan, selector, catalogs, secret targets) built from input once.
Owns plain host command execution under kernel custody with the JSON capture distinction stated once.
Owns the one selector resolver: a typed Route enum (task/builtin/exec alias/deferral) and nothing else decides where a selector goes; it runs nothing.
Owns standard-task host/container routing decisions, delegating to the exec routing owner with typed overrides; container-handoff short-circuit is explicit.

Owns selection resolution and fallback routes (built-in, exec alias, deferral), plus workspace-resolution validation before a fallback can run. Typed-fact deduction: the managed-mode check compares the manifest `mode` string.

Owns the one in-process sequence engine: step resolution, builtin/task/helper steps, progress and outcome. Deductions: a builtin step's typed command is recovered by re-parsing rendered argv, and step kinds are partly classified from command text.
Owns rendering and running a workspace-seeded task command, with the session-access note (access never travels in a rendered command) recorded at the source.
